Four used the separate position-65 point, two of which also tried the complete recorded feature-specific SQL listed below. Roles were cluster-global in these upgrade repeats. Their independent restore is covered by the encrypted prior-release exercise.

data_and_authority.prior_release: The original archive restored the private payload into another cluster and file store. The owner read its verified plaintext twice, the second subject made zero file reads, and the six missing/altered component cases and one foreign fence point were refused.
data_and_authority.repeated_checks: On every upgrade target, the two Auth identities, their link states and six scoped role profiles matched the dump source. The owner principal could read its ledger and private bytes. The other identity could not read the object. Anonymous payment/object access and a runtime financial update outside admission were denied. The later database copies used the same isolated fixture file store.
data_and_authority.existing_payment_reference: The seeded payment received the same 12-digit value on all six targets and the ALWAYS immutability trigger was enabled.

separate_payment_proof: The maintained payment-reference fixture passed three tests covering allocation, concurrent receipts, sequence-tail restore, search and non-reuse. That isolated fixture supplies a test operator function and a reduced retention inventory. The populated managed upgrade remains open.
required_for_full_replay: An authorized, independently restorable recovery point for the missing historical provider/commissioning state, with matching roles, Realtime metadata, vendor Storage history and retained function preimages, is needed to rehearse all 82 plus the seven pending migrations and their runtime consumers. This exercise made no provider or application requests.
